Add expert comments to a Delphi data object

Source: R/comments.R
delphi_add_comments.Rd

Attaches the written comments of the experts to a delphi_data object, so that each comment can be read next to the rating of its author and summarised by item, round and theme. Comments can be supplied in two layouts:

  • long (layout = "long", default): one row per comment, with columns for the expert, the item and the comment, and optionally the round, the indicator and the themes; this is the layout of the comments sheet of the template created by delphi_template();

  • wide (layout = "wide"): one row per expert and one comment column per item, as exported by many survey platforms.

Usage

delphi_add_comments(
  x,
  comments,
  layout = c("long", "wide"),
  expert_col = "expert",
  item_col = "item",
  comment_col = "comment",
  round_col = NULL,
  indicator_col = NULL,
  theme_col = NULL,
  round = NULL,
  comment_cols = NULL,
  items = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A delphi_data object.

comments

A data frame of comments.

layout

"long" (default) or "wide"; see Description.

expert_col

Name of the column with the expert identifiers, which must match those used for the ratings of the same round.

item_col, comment_col

For the long layout, names of the columns with the item code and the text of the comment. Comments with an empty item are treated as general comments on the questionnaire.

round_col, indicator_col, theme_col

For the long layout, names of the optional columns with the round, the indicator to which the comment refers and the themes coded by the researchers. By default, columns named round, indicator and theme are used when present (the round column only when round is not given).

round

Round of the comments, used when there is no round column. It can be omitted when x holds a single round.

comment_cols

For the wide layout, the comment columns, by name or position, one per item and in the same order as items.

items

For the wide layout, the items to which the comment columns refer. By default, all the items of x, in their order.

Value

x, with the comments stored in the element comments: a data frame with columns expert, round, item (NA for general comments), indicator (NA when the comment refers to the item as a whole), comment and theme (NA when not coded).

Details

Empty comments are ignored, and spaces and line breaks within a comment are collapsed into single spaces. Comments are matched to the ratings through the expert identifier and the round, also when the experts are not linked across rounds. A comment whose author has no rating in that round is kept, with a warning, but its position relative to the ratings of the panel cannot be determined.

Themes are short labels assigned by the researchers after reading the comments, as in a qualitative content analysis, for example "regulation" or "costs". Several themes can be assigned to the same comment by separating them with a semicolon ("regulation; costs"). The same theme must be written in the same way throughout. Themes are optional and are summarised by delphi_themes().

Calling the function again adds further comments, for example those of another round. Comments already stored are not duplicated.

See also

delphi_comments(), delphi_comment_counts(), delphi_themes(), delphi_words(); read_delphi() reads the comments from a sheet of the same Excel file.

Examples

r1 <- data.frame(expert = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
                 E1 = c(7, 8, 6, 2), E2 = c(3, 5, 4, 9))
x <- delphi_data(r1, expert_col = "expert", indicator = "impact")

# Long layout: one row per comment
cm <- data.frame(
  expert = c("A", "D", "D", "B"),
  item = c("E1", "E1", "E2", NA),
  comment = c("Depends on public funding.",
              "Unlikely without new regulation.",
              "The statement is too broad.",
              "Clear questionnaire."),
  theme = c("funding", "regulation", "wording", NA)
)
x <- delphi_add_comments(x, cm)
delphi_comments(x)
#> <delphi_comments> 4 comment(s)
#> 
#> Round 1, item E1
#>   [A]: impact within IQR (theme: funding)
#>     Depends on public funding.
#>   [D]: impact below Q1 (theme: regulation)
#>     Unlikely without new regulation.
#> 
#> Round 1, item E2
#>   [D]: impact above Q3 (theme: wording)
#>     The statement is too broad.
#> 
#> Round 1, general comments
#>   [B]
#>     Clear questionnaire.

# Wide layout: one comment column per item
wide <- data.frame(expert = c("A", "C"),
                   c_E1 = c("Depends on public funding.", ""),
                   c_E2 = c(NA, "Hard to assess."))
y <- delphi_data(r1, expert_col = "expert", indicator = "impact")
y <- delphi_add_comments(y, wide, layout = "wide",
                         comment_cols = c("c_E1", "c_E2"))
y$comments
#>   expert round item indicator                    comment theme
#> 1      A     1   E1      <NA> Depends on public funding.  <NA>
#> 2      C     1   E2      <NA>            Hard to assess.  <NA>
